blocks.text: Buying a 55+ Age-Restricted Condo in Maple Ridge, BC

parts.t: Maple Ridge's 55+ apartment buildings offer lock-and-leave convenience, elevator access, secure underground parking, and social clubhouses right in the flat walkable core of Town Centre (East Central) and West Central. Residents are steps from the Maple Ridge Seniors Activity Centre (12150 224 St), pharmacies, medical clinics, Haney Place Mall, and the Maple Ridge Leisure Centre.

Because 55+ condos restrict occupancy to older adults under the BC Strata Property Act, they typically trade at a lower price-per-square-foot than unrestricted buildings—allowing retirees and downsizers to purchase spacious 900-to-1,200+ sq ft two-bedroom suites while freeing up equity from a family home.

blocks.text: Evaluating 55+ Condo Buildings: Elevators, Scooters, Fees & CRF

parts.t: When touring 55+ condos in Maple Ridge, we check whether the building has one or two elevators (and recent elevator modernization history), wide hallways and barrier-free entryways, mobility scooter parking/charging rules in the parkade, what utilities are included in the monthly strata fee (such as gas, hot water, or radiant heat), and the Contingency Reserve Fund balance.

Why are 55+ condos in Maple Ridge often more affordable than all-ages condos?

Because 55+ buildings require at least one or all occupants (depending on the specific bylaw and statutory exemptions) to be aged 55 or older, the buyer pool is narrower than unrestricted buildings—often giving 55+ buyers larger floor plans for the price.
Are 55+ condo age restrictions still valid under BC law?

Yes. When British Columbia amended the Strata Property Act via Bill 44, it preserved the right of strata corporations to enforce 55+ age-restriction bylaws while removing younger age limits such as 19+ or 45+.
Where is the Maple Ridge Seniors Activity Centre?

The Maple Ridge Seniors Activity Centre (operated by the Ridge Meadows Seniors Society) is located at 12150 224 Street in East Central, offering fitness classes, hot lunches, social clubs, and workshops within walking distance of Town Centre condos.
What do monthly strata fees typically include in 55+ Maple Ridge condos?

Monthly strata fees cover building insurance, elevator maintenance, common area housekeeping, landscaping, garbage/recycling, and Contingency Reserve Fund contributions; many 55+ buildings also include natural gas (for fireplace/heating) and hot water.
Can a younger family member own a 55+ condo for a senior parent?

Yes. BC's 55+ strata bylaws regulate the age of the occupants living in the unit, not the age of the registered owner on title—so an adult child can hold title or co-sign a mortgage for a parent aged 55 or older who lives in the suite.
